name: What is the difference between a salt-based water softener and a salt-free water conditioner?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a salt-based water softener and a salt-free water conditioner?

acceptedAnswer.text: Salt-based water softeners actively remove hardness minerals (calcium and magnesium) from the water through ion exchange, typically resulting in noticeably softer water and elimination of scale buildup. Salt-free water conditioners, also known as descalers, don't remove minerals but rather alter their crystalline structure to prevent them from sticking to surfaces. A practical tradeoff is that softeners provide truly soft water benefits like better soap lather and protection for appliances, while conditioners are often lower maintenance but may not deliver the same 'soft water' feel or complete scale prevention.
acceptedAnswer.description: Salt-based softeners remove minerals for soft water, while salt-free conditioners alter minerals to prevent scale. Softeners offer more comprehensive benefits but conditioners are lower maintenance.
